assertions.name: bar_fixes_the_bracket_and_swaps_the_bonds
assertions.note: so invariance of w.b_pp + (1-w).b_nn reduces to (1 - wbar - w)(b_pp - b_nn) = 0, i.e. wbar = 1 - w for q != 1. ONE equation, not a determination

assertions.name: every_member_is_bar_invariant
assertions.note: wbar_k = q^k/[2]_{q^k} = 1 - w_k identically. Lean: bar_weight_bar_eq_one_sub, proved for all real k

assertions.name: the_corpus_rule_is_the_k_equals_zero_member
assertions.note: w_0 = 1/2. Nothing selects it except the unstated extra assumption that w carries no q -- an undeformed bracket inside a deformed algebra

assertions.name: and_w_one_is_the_crossing_weight
assertions.note: w_1 = q^-1/[2]_q = 1/(q^2+1), which lands exactly on the geometric mean 1/[2]_q. Lean: weight_one plus SymmetrySignAmGm.crossing_weight

assertions.name: the_sign_is_wrong_below_k_one_and_SEMF_above_it
assertions.note: w_k is strictly decreasing in k (Lean: weight_strictAnti) and w_1 is the geometric mean, so k > 1 is exactly the region below it. This is the DERIVED bound; k itself is not

assertions.name: and_delta_is_odd_about_k_one
assertions.note: delta(w_(1-t)) = -delta(w_(1+t)). The corpus at k = 0 has k = 2 as its exact mirror, -0.021618 against +0.021618 -- the same reflection the power means show about the geometric mean

parameters.note: k is NOT derived here and nothing is wired to production; the derived content is the bound delta > 0 <=> k > 1
